detail.abstract: This paper reports a designed-for-test measurement of brand visibility in large language model (LLM) outputs for Bed Bath & Beyond (BBB), thirty-seven months after the brand's Chapter 11 bankruptcy and online-only revival under post-acquisition ownership. Pier 1-a smaller-footprint structural comparator with the same fate type but seventy months post-collapse-was added to the household-goods registry. Eight hypotheses with explicit numerical thresholds were committed to a pre-registration document locked on 4 May 2026 prior to any data collection. The measurement comprised six prompts × six models × eight runs (n = 288 successful measurements after a pre-registered failed-call recovery cycle) across model lineups from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and xAI. BBB's aggregate raw AI Presence was 38.2 percent, with a cross-model spread of 41.6 percentage points; Pier 1 surfaced at 0.0 percent across the same prompts and models. Six of eight pre-registered hypotheses were confirmed at the raw-rate level. Manual valence review of every BBB mention (88 percent strict inter-rater agreement on a stratified 25-row spot-check audit) reframes the result: the naive-phantom rate is 1.7 percent, and 88 percent of BBB mentions are surfaced with disclaimer indicating awareness of the entity change. The paper develops recommendationslot persistence-the proposition that brand-mention pathways become reinforcement-encoded structures that persist beyond entity changes-as a candidate hypothesis adjacent to but structurally distinct from existing AI-Surfacing hypotheses. The reframe is exploratory; construct validity remains open and is the proposed object of a Phase 3 designed-for-confirmation study.

detail.abstract: This study examines the factors influencing audience engagement in esports events in France. The research focuses on four independent variables, including streaming quality, social media interaction, event experience, and team popularity, and their effects on audience engagement. A quantitative research approach was adopted using an online questionnaire distributed to esports audiences in France. A total of 541 valid responses were collected and analyzed using SPSS software. The study employed descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings indicate that team popularity has the strongest positive influence on audience engagement, while event experience shows a significant but negative relationship. Streaming quality and social media interaction were not found to significantly influence audience engagement. The study contributes to a better understanding of esports audience behavior and provides practical recommendations for esports organizers and marketers in France.

detail.abstract: A Indústria 4.0 não está apenas transformando máquinas — está redefinindo o papel das lideranças. Na entrevista conduzida por Luiz Cláudio Zenone com Léo Bruno no podcast O Marketeiro, fica evidente que o maior desafio das organizações não é tecnológico, mas humano. Automação, dados e digitalização exigem líderes mais adaptáveis, colaborativos e orientados ao desenvolvimento de pessoas, porém ainda persistem modelos centralizadores, resistentes à mudança e desconectados da nova realidade. O contraste é claro: enquanto setores como o agronegócio avançam com inovação e eficiência, muitas organizações permanecem presas a culturas ultrapassadas. O futuro não será liderado por quem domina apenas a técnica, mas por quem equilibra competências, influencia pessoas e constrói ambientes capazes de evoluir continuamente.

title: THE EXPERIENCE HELIX™ : From Service Blueprints to Predictive CX-DNA A Framework for Real-Time Customer Experience Satisfaction Prediction Using Knowledge Graphs and Graph Neural Networks

detail.title: THE EXPERIENCE HELIX™ : From Service Blueprints to Predictive CX-DNA A Framework for Real-Time Customer Experience Satisfaction Prediction Using Knowledge Graphs and Graph Neural Networks
detail.abstract:
This whitepaper introduces The Experience Helix™, a proprietary framework designed to evolve traditional, static service blueprints into dynamic, real-time intelligence systems. While standard CX management relies on retrospective, lagging indicators like CSAT, this framework utilizes Customer Digital DNA (CX-DNA)—a high-dimensional knowledge graph to predict customer sentiment as it happens.

The Methodology : The Experience Helix transforms the flat layers of a service blueprint into a network of five node types (Customer, Touchpoint, Operational, Resource, and System) connected by three weighted edge categories (Temporal, Causal, and Financial). Using Graph Neural Networks (GNN) and iterative message-passing, the framework computes a Predictive Customer Experience Satisfaction Score (pCXSAT).

Key Contributions : Real-Time Intervention: A three-tier framework (Green, Amber, Red zones) that triggers automated escalation or service recovery during the interactions; Strategic Simulation: A "CEO Dashboard" capability allowing executives to perform sensitivity analysis and project ROI on operational investments before committing resources.; Calibration & Governance: A rigorous validation loop using Huber loss to refine model weights against actual outcomes, alongside a four-principle ethical governance framework (Transparency, Consent, Equity, and Boundaries). By shifting from reactive problem-solving to proactive, predictive modeling, the Experience Helix provides an 18-month implementation roadmap for organizations to transition from documenting "intended" journeys to managing "lived" experiences.

title: Why You Do What You Do: Understanding Behaviour Ecosystem: A Scholarly Extract Introducing The Vedic Behavioural Stack™

detail.title: Why You Do What You Do: Understanding Behaviour Ecosystem: A Scholarly Extract Introducing The Vedic Behavioural Stack™

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a conceptual work and does not involve human participants, animal subjects, or primary data collection. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Human behaviour is often interpreted too narrowly through the language of willpower, discipline, personality, or isolated choice. Such explanations remain incomplete because they understate the layered conditions under which behaviour actually emerges. This scholarly extract introduces The Vedic Behavioural Stack™, a behavioural systems framework that explains action as the outcome of interacting internal states, embodied capacity, identity protection, stored behavioural momentum, and timing conditions.

The framework is organized around five interacting layers: Prakriti, referring to embodied behavioural capacity and tolerance; Guna, referring to dynamic force states that influence activation, clarity, and inertia; Antahkarana, referring to the internal behavioural machinery through which perception, evaluation, identity anchoring, and continuity operate; Samskara, referring to stored behavioural impressions and carried momentum; and Kala, referring to timing, rhythm, and behavioural windows. Taken together, these layers offer a systems-based account of why individuals may know what to do yet fail to act, repeat patterns they consciously reject, or shift behaviour under stress, fatigue, criticism, or environmental pressure.

Rather than presenting behaviour as a moral event, this framework treats it as an emergent outcome shaped by interacting conditions. The extract positions The Vedic Behavioural Stack™ as a conceptual contribution with potential relevance to behavioural science, consumer behaviour, leadership studies, digital environments, health communication, and habit research. It also identifies possible directions for future empirical validation and interdisciplinary application.

title: Three Ways to Fail to Conclude: A Null-report on Large Language Model Citation Claims for Brazilian Brands (N = 7,052, 12 days)

detail.title: Three Ways to Fail to Conclude: A Null-report on Large Language Model Citation Claims for Brazilian Brands (N = 7,052, 12 days)

declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects were involved. Data was generated by querying public large language model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity) under each provider's terms of service. No personally identifiable information was collected; brand names used in the cohort are public. Ethics review was not required. See the paper's Ethics section for full disclosure.

detail.abstract:
Background. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) has emerged as a practitioner discipline asserting a growing list of causal claims about how large language models (LLMs) cite brands-which architectures cite more, how robust commercial models are to fictitious entities, and whether citation universes across models diverge enough to demand per-LLM optimization strategies. Rigorous empirical evidence in Brazilian Portuguese, and under multi-vertical production constraints, remains scarce. Methods. We collected 7,052 LLM responses over 12 consecutive days (2026-03-24 to 2026-04-22) probing 69 entities (61 real brands and 8 fictitious decoy entities designed for false-positive calibration) across 4 verticals (fintech, retail, health, technology) against 4 production LLMs (OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, Google gemini-2.5-pro, Perplexity sonar). Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile was onboarded mid-collection and excluded from confirmatory analysis. We formulate three hypotheses popularly asserted in the Brazilian GEO market and analyse them under Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, BCa bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 resamples), and cluster-robust standard errors by collection day. Results. The aggregate citation rate is 77.62% (95% BCa CI [76.62%, 78.57%]). For all three focal hypotheses we fail to reject the null-but by independent mechanisms. H1 (RAG advantage) fails through statistical underpower (difference-2.58 pp, 95% CI crosses zero, p = 0.067 naive → p ≈ 0.48 cluster-robust; Cohen's h =-0.061). H2 (hallucination robustness) fails through methodological design (the fictitious probe was never activated during production collection, so a Rule-of-Three upper bound of 0.043% reflects absence of spontaneous hallucination on legitimate queries, not adversarial resistance). H3 (disjoint cross-LLM citation universes) fails through
instrumentation (three of the four LLMs emit effectively no structured source data, rendering Jaccard comparison a measure of instrumentation rather than agreement). Vertical heterogeneity (Cramér’s V = 0.23, p < 10−82) and
Portuguese–English divergence (h = 0.136, p < 10−8) do survive correction and subsampling. Significance for agentic commerce. The three claims examined are no longer academic. Contemporaneous work formalises autonomous LLM agents
as buyer-seller negotiators (Liu et al., 2026), as agentic purchasers that refine preferences conversationally before recommending assortments (Cao and Hu, 2026), and as cross-layer economic actors with a catalogued attack surface
(Mao et al., 2026). In each of these regimes, which brands an LLM cites ceases to be a metadatum and becomes an economic selection signal. The present null-report therefore bounds from below the evidence currently available to calibrate the very systems that such agents will run on top of.
Conclusion. We present this as a null-report with diagnostic value: the same dataset simultaneously licenses descriptive claims about linguistic and vertical surface heterogeneity while refusing three architectural claims that commercially matter to the GEO market. We release preregistration, code and data for adversarial replication.

title: Digital Content, Buyer Trust and Inquiry Progression in B2B Industrial Markets: A Mechanism-Building Study

detail.title: Digital Content, Buyer Trust and Inquiry Progression in B2B Industrial Markets: A Mechanism-Building Study
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how public digital content supports buyer evaluation, value interpretation, trust reinforcement and inquiry progression in B2B industrial markets. It focuses in particular on how content moves beyond lead generation and becomes part of the buyer's own evaluation work. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a qualitative mechanism-building design. Evidence is drawn from four publicly observable B2B industrial cases, 1,627 anonymized buyer inquiry records from an export-oriented electrical equipment supplier, three supplementary practitioner interviews and micro-level social-video interaction records. The inquiry records are used descriptively to examine progression stages, and no deterministic causal link is claimed between a single content item and an individual inquiry. Findings: The evidence points to two linked mechanisms: value translation and trust reinforcement. In the cases examined, technical content appears to matter when buyers can connect it with project concerns such as reliability, compliance, operational fit, cost reduction and risk control. Public content also appears to serve as buyer-side evaluative infrastructure, since it can be found, revisited and used to check supplier credibility both before and after inquiry submission. From this perspective, an inquiry marks the beginning of a stage-gated evaluation process rather than the end of conversion. Practical implications: B2B industrial marketers should avoid judging digital platforms only by traffic or inquiry volume. More useful practice may involve designing content around buyer journeys, building public trust assets, recording inquiry progression stages and assessing lead quality through the depth of buyer interaction. Originality/value: This study develops the idea of value translation, frames public digital content as part of a supplier's trust infrastructure, and redefines inquiry in B2B industrial sales as a progression process rather than merely a captured lead.

detail.abstract:
Purpose: Prior research highlights the negative consequences of debt aversion which can constrain tertiary education, home ownership, liquidity management, and broader financial decision-making. The goals of this research are therefore to document the extent of debt aversion in the Anglosphere by product, to develop a suitable measure of debt attitudes that can be applied across products, and to determine the correlates of debt attitudes and debt aversion. 
Design/methodology: We investigate debt aversion among young adults in Australia and the United Kingdom using a cross-sectional survey of 1,025 respondents spanning 14 debt products. 
Findings: Even the most accepted product, home loans, attracts avoidance in a significant minority (14-24% of participants), with some products attracting avoidance rates of more than 70% (informal debt from family and friends, personal loans, payday loans). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses identify two attitude dimensions: an investment-oriented dimension associated with asset-building debt, such as home loans, and an expense buffering dimension linked to consumption-smoothing credit, such as BNPL (buy-now-paylater). 
Practical implications: We discuss implications for product design and for policymakers, with a focus on home loans and BNPL. 
Originality: Our new measure of debt attitudes can be applied across products. Frugality and debt literacy are negatively associated with buffering attitudes, while social norms and risk tolerance are positively associated with both attitude dimensions. Debt attitudes and their correlates play a central role in explaining debt aversion.

detail.abstract: Generative AI is collapsing brand consideration sets, in many categories, into a single recommendation returned against paraphrased intent-fundamentally altering how brands enter or fail to enter consumer choice. The substrate introduces a paradox: the same mechanism that amplifies incumbent advantage through training-corpus prominence also creates the only systematic conditions under which that advantage is disrupted. This article extends the Ehrenberg-Bass framework by introducing AI availability-the propensity of a brand to be surfaced by generative AI against paraphrased consumer intent-as a third dimension of retrieval, and formalises the paradox that defines its operation. A unifying proposition (P0) specifies the mechanism: training-corpus prominence interacting with single-recommendation output. Two outcome propositions specify reinforcement of incumbent hierarchies in the modal case (P1) and selective suspension under jointly-met conditionsutilitarian category, low identity load, single-recommendation interface, AI-trusting consumer (P2). Two moderators (identity load; brand familiarity) bound the conditions (P3, P4). The framework operates on existing brand-equity assets in the present configuration, with pathways to partial displacement specified for agentic configurations. An experiment (n = 208) demonstrates a 25.4 percentage-point choice shift consistent with the suspension prediction. Three operational tools translate the framework into brand-portfolio practice.

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on managerial decision-making and organizational performance within a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) operating in the digital services sector. Using a dataset of 50 decision incidents from 2022 to 2024, the research compares AI-assisted decisions with traditional human-led decisions across key performance indicators, including return on investment (ROI), customer acquisition cost (CAC), lead conversion rate, decision speed, and decision accuracy. The findings reveal that AI-assisted decisions consistently outperform non-AI decisions in terms of efficiency, cost optimization, and outcome consistency, particularly in data-intensive areas such as pricing, budget allocation, and lead management. However, mixed results are observed in promotion-related decisions, where external market factors and strategic intuition play a significant role. The study concludes that AI functions most effectively as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for human judgment, enhancing organizational performance when combined with managerial oversight. These findings contribute to the limited empirical literature on AI adoption in SMEs and provide practical insights for firms seeking to integrate AI into decision-making processes.

detail.abstract: Most international retail expansions fail not in the market—but before entry. The strategic error is not poor localisation. It is an absence of balanced adaptation: the disciplined ability to identify precisely what must never change—the secret sauce that makes the economics work—and to adapt everything else to what the market structurally demands. Retailers that cannot draw that line before entry will have it drawn for them, expensively, after.

detail.abstract: ABSTRACT (English): This note introduces the first edition of an annual sectoral barometer of e-commerce trust in France, based on the analysis of 30,861 verified consumer reviews aggregated across 580,500 French companies between January 2024 and April 2026. Each review is tied to a transaction identifier and weighted on four dimensions (recency, statistical volume, source verification by transaction ID, author profile coherence). The weighted average score across all sectors is 3.8 out of 5, that is, 0.5 point below the unweighted averages commonly displayed on Anglo-Saxon platforms. Six structural findings emerge: (1) detected fraud concentrates on six sectors (retail forex, dropshipping, paid online dating, coaching, online psychic services, dietary supplements) representing 18% of volume but 62% of suspect signals; (2) gaps between unweighted and weighted scores reach 1.2 point in high-fraud sectors; (3) recency is underused by mainstream algorithms; (4) fraud is geographically concentrated in three regions (Ile-de-France, PACA, Hauts-de-France); (5) brands under citizen boycott campaigns score 0.4 point lower in verified reviews; (6) the transparency premium (response rate) is measurable. Datasets are released under Open Licence 2.0 on data.gouv.fr. RESUME (Francais) : Cette note presente la premiere edition d'un barometre annuel de la confiance e-commerce en France, fonde sur l'analyse de 30 861 avis clients verifies agreges sur 580 500 entreprises francaises entre janvier 2024 et avril 2026. Six enseignements structurels emergent de l'analyse : la fraude detectee se concentre sur six secteurs (forex retail, dropshipping, rencontres en ligne payantes, coaching, voyance, complements alimentaires) qui representent 18 % du volume mais 62 % des signaux suspects ; les ecarts entre score brut et score pondere atteignent 1,2 point sur les secteurs a forte fraude ; la recence est sous-utilisee par les algorithmes classiques ; la fraude est concentree geographiquement sur trois regions (Ile-de-France, PACA, Hauts-de-France) ; les marques sous campagne citoyenne ont un score d'avis verifies inferieur de 0,4 point en moyenne ; la prime a la transparence (taux de reponse aux avis) est mesurable. title: Global Export Strategy for Bhadohi Carpets: Leveraging Tradition, Technology, and E-Commerce for International Market Expansion

detail.title: Global Export Strategy for Bhadohi Carpets: Leveraging Tradition, Technology, and E-Commerce for International Market Expansion
detail.abstract:
This paper explores the export potential of Bhadohi carpets under the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative, focusing on their transformation from a traditional craft into a globally competitive product. Bhadohi, known as the “Carpet City of India,” contributes significantly to India’s carpet exports, supported by its GI-tagged heritage and skilled artisan base. The study analyzes domestic and international market demand, target customer segments, and key export destinations such as the USA, Germany, and the UAE.
The paper further examines a dual-channel export strategy involving both online platforms (Amazon Global, Etsy, D2C websites) and offline channels (trade fairs, distributors, and B2B partnerships). It highlights the role of branding, sustainable packaging, and certifications in enhancing global competitiveness. Additionally, the integration of artificial intelligence in design, demand forecasting, quality control, and digital marketing is discussed as a critical enabler of efficiency and scalability.
Challenges such as high logistics costs, lack of export knowledge, and international competition are identified, along with practical solutions including government support, digital adoption, and strategic pricing. The study concludes that with the right combination of heritage value, technology adoption, and export infrastructure, Bhadohi carpets have strong potential to capture premium global markets while ensuring sustainable livelihoods for artisans.

detail.abstract: The purpose of the study is to measure the motivation and satisfaction of the tourists visiting a nature-based tourism destination. It is an exploratory and descriptive research where hypotheses are tested. Primary data was collected from the tourist respondents, including both Indian and foreign tourists who visited Mudumalai Wildlife Sanctuary, a prominent nature-based tourism destination, through a structured questionnaire. The overall survey tool reliability value is 0.871. A total of 400 respondents were administered the questionnaire, of which 360 were Indian tourists, and 40 were foreign tourists. Primary data were analyzed using Independent Sample t-test, Factor Analysis, Mean ranking, Correlations, One-way ANOVA, and Linear Regression. Tourist motivation was influenced by factors like Attractions, Accommodation, Transportation, Amenities and community benefits. Accordingly, tourist satisfactions were influenced by factors like Activities and Attractions. The study revealed that tourist motivation and tourist satisfaction are negatively associated and negatively correlated with each other. The insights of the study have significant theoretical and managerial implications for product development and destination marketing.

title: Faith, Flesh, and Function: A Systematic Review of Religious Perspectives On Speech Therapy Implants and the Ethics of Technological Mediation
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University and Kwame Nkrumah University

detail.title: Faith, Flesh, and Function: A Systematic Review of Religious Perspectives On Speech Therapy Implants and the Ethics of Technological Mediation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for the preparation of this work.

detail.abstract: This systematic review examines how four major religious traditions, Judaism, Islam, Buddhism, and Roman Catholicism, frame the ethics of speech therapy implants, including cochlear implants and neurological biochips. Drawing on PRISMA guidelines, we analysed 42 peer-reviewed articles, doctrinal texts, and theological commentaries published between 2000 and 2025. Three intersecting themes organise the findings: the body as a moral object, the tension between healing and human identity, and the limits of technological intervention. Across traditions, a permissive orientation toward restorative technologies coexists with serious reservations about enhancement, cultural erasure, and the reduction of persons to their functional utility. Crucially, the Deaf community's resistance to cochlear implants introduces a layer of ethical complexity that religious frameworks have only partially addressed. Speechlanguage pathologists practising in religiously diverse contexts must develop spiritual literacy and integrate culturally responsive frameworks into their clinical reasoning. The paper argues that religious ethics offers clinicians a normative vocabulary that moves beyond purely biomedical assessment toward a holistic account of what it means to heal.

title: Bridging Legal Systems: Anti-Corruption Compliance Frameworks in the Brazilian Construction Industry and Their Implications for U.S.-Based Multinational Operations

detail.title: Bridging Legal Systems: Anti-Corruption Compliance Frameworks in the Brazilian Construction Industry and Their Implications for U.S.-Based Multinational Operations
detail.abstract: This article examines the intersection of Brazilian anti-corruption law-specifically Law No. 12,846/2013 (the Brazilian Clean Companies Act) and its implementing decrees-with the compliance obligations of U.S.-based multinational corporations operating in Brazil's construction and infrastructure sectors. Drawing on practical experience implementing compliance programs for one of Brazil's largest engineering conglomerates, this piece analyzes how robust local compliance frameworks reduce legal exposure for American companies contracting with Brazilian partners, mitigate risk under the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), and create measurable value for cross-border transactions. The author argues that professionals with hybrid expertise in Brazilian and U.S. legal systems occupy a uniquely critical role in facilitating compliant, commercially viable partnerships-an expertise that directly serves the national interests of the United States in promoting anti-corruption standards in emerging markets.

title:
Neural Arbitration Framework  (NAF)
A Conceptual Architecture and Research Agenda for Epistemic Arbitration in Large Language Models

detail.title:
Neural Arbitration Framework  (NAF)
A Conceptual Architecture and Research Agenda for Epistemic Arbitration in Large Language Models
detail.abstract:
Large language models exhibit a structural bias toward narrative closure in zones of incomplete training, generating fluent, coherent responses where epistemic uncertainty should prevail. This paper argues that this phenomenon, commonly described as hallucination, is functionally analogous — at the level of behavior under incomplete information — to the confabulatory behavior of the left hemisphere in split-brain patients, as documented by Gazzaniga and Sperry: a cognitive system optimized for coherence fills gaps without internal awareness of doing so. 

The Neural Arbitration Framework (NAF) proposes that this bias is not an external defect correctable by verification layers but an architectural consequence: current language systems lack the functional separation between a generative mode and an epistemic mode, and the arbitration protocol that determines which one holds the floor. The solution does not necessarily require external verification as the primary mechanism, but rather the formalization of two complementary cognitive modes, structurally analogous to the hemispheric duality of the human brain, governed by an arbitration protocol with interruptive authority over narrative closure. 

The NAF's distinctive claim is not merely temporal but functional: the epistemic process has interruptive authority over narrative closure. The NAF does not necessarily introduce new signals; it introduces a new functional organization of signals already explored in the literature — converting uncertainty estimation, abstention, verification, and self-correction into a unified arbitration protocol with explicit interruptive authority over the generative process and structured accumulation of cognitive deficits.

title: Shadow AI and the Security Ownership Gap: A Conceptual Framework for Governing Ungoverned AI in the Enterprise Introducing the Shadow AI Risk Governance Framework (SARGF)

detail.title: Shadow AI and the Security Ownership Gap: A Conceptual Framework for Governing Ungoverned AI in the Enterprise Introducing the Shadow AI Risk Governance Framework (SARGF)
detail.abstract:
Organisations are rapidly integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into their operations, decision processes, and customer-facing services. However, a substantial and growing share of enterprise AI use is occurring outside the reach of formal security, risk management, and accountability frameworks. We are calling this ‘Shadow AI’, and a related construct — the ‘AI Security Ownership Gap’ — is the condition in which responsibility for AI-related cybersecurity risk is not clearly assigned, not handled consistently, and contested across the organisational functions whose cooperation would be needed to manage it. Taking our ideas from the well-understood world of ‘Shadow IT’ (and what happens when people use tech without approval), current examples of AI being misused and data leaks, and from established ways of managing AI (like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, and the NIS2 Directive) we are saying that the protections we have now rely on knowing about and listing all systems. By their nature, they cannot control AI that no one ever asked permission for.

Because of this, we have developed the Shadow AI Risk Governance Framework (SARGF). It is a way of thinking about things, with three pillars: getting to know the AI and what it is doing, figuring out who is responsible for it, and providing the tools to make things work. We are looking at Shadow AI governance as something for managers to deal with, not just the IT department, and giving a common language for the Chief Information Security Officer, the Chief Technology Officer, Data Protection Officer and heads of the different parts of the business to work together. We illustrate how SARGF works in a business. And we are now researching SARGF, testing it with a series of studies in European companies, using both quantitative and qualitative methods. This document sets out the ideas behind it, and we will share the actual tests we used, how we confirmed it, and what we found in later publications.

title: Export Documentation

detail.title: Export Documentation
detail.abstract:
Export documentation is a crucial part of international trade that ensures smooth movement of goods across borders. It includes commercial, regulatory, transport, and financial documents required for legal compliance, customs clearance, and payment security. Proper documentation helps in reducing risks, avoiding delays, and ensuring transparency in export transactions.

With the advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), export documentation has become faster and more efficient. AI helps in document automation, error detection, fraud prevention, and compliance management. It reduces human errors, saves time, and improves accuracy in global trade processes.

title: Trade, Tariffs, and Wealth in 15 th Century Bruges

detail.title: Trade, Tariffs, and Wealth in 15 th Century Bruges

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest
declarations.funderStatement: There is no external funding

detail.abstract: International trade generates substantial welfare gains through specialization according to relative comparative advantages. This enables nations to consume beyond autarky production by allocating resources toward activities of most relative efficiency. Three canonical mechanisms govern these outcomes: Ricardian comparative advantage, which demonstrates that mutually beneficial exchange does not require absolute productivity superiority; trade barriers, which generate deadweight welfare losses by distorting resource allocation; and exchange rate movements, whereby currency depreciation improves export competitiveness. Fifteenth-century Bruges constitutes an exemplary historical exemplification of these mechanisms. As Northwestern Europe's preeminent international trading hub, the city developed commercial infrastructure that concentrated buyers, sellers, and financial instruments, reducing transaction costs and generating economies of scale. Staple rights, requiring imported goods to be offered locally prior to re-export, constituted a trade barrier partially distorting these gains, while regularly published currency exchange rates mitigated the uncertainty otherwise associated with multi-currency commerce. These institutional arrangements generated immense wealth for the Burgundian state. Part of the trade constituted luxury goods including rare and costly pigments such as ultramarine from Afghanistan or vermilion from Spain, without which the chromatic splendour of early Flemish masters such as Jan van Eyck would have been unattainable. The central lesson of this chapter is that open and well-governed trade frameworks-then as now-remain a precondition for both material prosperity and lasting cultural achievement.

Abstract

La crisis energética actual, caracterizada por su complejidad multidimensional, demanda enfoques innovadores que trasciendan las limitaciones de los paradigmas tradicionales de resolución de problemas. Este artículo explora cómo la innovación, concebida como un marco de trabajo flexible y dinámico, se posiciona como una herramienta indispensable para abordar los desafíos sistémicos asociados a la transición energética, el cambio climático y las dinámicas geopolíticas. A través de un análisis riguroso, se destaca la capacidad de la innovación para integrar perspectivas interdisciplinarias, fomentar la adaptabilidad frente a escenarios volátiles y diseñar soluciones que transformen tanto las estructuras subyacentes como los modelos operativos en el sector energético. Asimismo, se examinan casos emblemáticos que ilustran cómo las soluciones innovadoras han permitido no solo mitigar los impactos de la crisis energética, sino también abrir nuevas oportunidades en términos de sostenibilidad y resiliencia. Este marco plantea la necesidad de un cambio de paradigma, en el cual la innovación no solo resuelva problemas inmediatos, sino que configure una visión estratégica para un sistema energético sostenible, inclusivo y robusto ante los retos del futuro.

Abstract

The current energy crisis, marked by its multidimensional complexity, demands innovative approaches that transcend the limitations of traditional problem-solving paradigms. This article explores how innovation, conceived as a flexible and dynamic framework, emerges as an indispensable tool for addressing the systemic challenges associated with energy transition, climate change, and geopolitical dynamics. Through rigorous analysis, it highlights innovation's capacity to integrate interdisciplinary perspectives, foster adaptability in volatile scenarios, and design solutions that transform both underlying structures and operational models in the energy sector. Furthermore, it examines emblematic cases illustrating how innovative solutions have not only mitigated the impacts of the energy crisis but also unlocked new opportunities in terms of sustainability and resilience. This framework calls for a paradigm shift where innovation not only resolves immediate challenges but also shapes a strategic vision for a sustainable, inclusive, and robust energy system capable of meeting future demands.

title: ROBUSTNESS MEASURES IN DISTRIBUTIONALLY ROBUST OPTIMIZATION
affiliations: Chuo University - Department of Data Science for Business Innovation, Sauder School of Business, University of British Columbia and National University of Singapore (NUS) - Department of Decision Sciences

detail.title: ROBUSTNESS MEASURES IN DISTRIBUTIONALLY ROBUST OPTIMIZATION
detail.abstract: Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) is a worst-case approach to decision making when there is model uncertainty. It is also well known that for certain uncertainty sets, DRO is approximated by a regularized nominal problem. We show that the regularizer is not just a penalty function but the worst-case sensitivity (WCS) of the expected cost with respect to deviations from the nominal model, giving it the interpretation of a robustness measure. This has substantial consequences for robust modeling. It shows that DRO is fundamentally a tradeoff between performance and robustness, where the robustness measure is determined by the uncertainty set. The robustness measure reveals properties of a cost distribution that affect sensitivity to misspecification. This leads to a systematic approach to selecting uncertainty sets. The family of DRO solutions obtained by varying the size of the uncertainty set traces a near Pareto-optimal performance-robustness frontier that can be used to select its size. The frontier identifies problem instances where the price of robustness is high and provides insight into effective ways of redesigning the system to reduce this cost. We derive WCS for a collection of commonly used uncertainty sets, and illustrate these ideas in a number of applications.

title:
The Unified Execution System
Binding Execution, Finality, and Verification into Deterministic Financial Infrastructure

detail.title:
The Unified Execution System
Binding Execution, Finality, and Verification into Deterministic Financial Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with Avid Innovations LLC. The research presented in this paper reflects independent conceptual and architectural work and was conducted without external financial influence.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work is theoretical and conceptual in nature and did not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental interventions requiring ethics approval.

detail.abstract:
Modern financial systems are built on structural assumptions: that clearly defined rules, ownership frameworks, and contractual conditions are sufficient to ensure reliable outcomes. In practice, these systems consistently fail at the moment that matters most-the point of execution-where participant behavior, shifting incentives, and real-time uncertainty determine whether execution remains aligned with intended outcomes under changing conditions. 

This paper introduces a unified systems framework that reconceptualizes financial infrastructure around three inseparable functions: execution, finality, and verification. Rather than treating these as independent layers or sequential processes, we define them as components of a single deterministic system responsible for producing, enforcing, and validating outcomes in real time. 

We show that execution is not guaranteed by structure, but must be actively governed at the behavioral level; that finality is not achieved through agreement or recording but through the elimination of all competing states; and that truth is not assumed through enforcement but verified as a system-level condition in which no alternative outcome can exist. 

From this foundation, we introduce the concept of a Unified Execution System-a closed-loop architecture in which execution, finality, and verification operate simultaneously to ensure that outcomes are not only produced, but made exclusive and confirmed as the only valid system state. 

This framework provides a new lens for understanding systemic failure in financial infrastructure and offers a path toward deterministic, outcome-driven systems capable of guaranteeing reliability at scale-even under conditions where traditional systems degrade into uncertainty.

title: Why They Give at the Office: Shareholder Welfare and Corporate Philanthropy in the Contractual Theory of the Corporation
affiliations: George Mason University - Antonin Scalia Law School and

detail.title: Why They Give at the Office: Shareholder Welfare and Corporate Philanthropy in the Contractual Theory of the Corporation
detail.abstract:
For centuries legal, political, social, and economic commentators have debated corporate social responsibility ad nauseam. An important component of that debate concerns the legitimacy of corporate philanthropy. Courts largely have resolved the legal issue in favor of allowing corporate management wide latitude in making philanthropic contributions. Yet there remains considerable controversy over whether corporate managers should have the authority to engage in these acts. Indeed, one reads more and more about the “problem of corporate philanthropy.”

It is ironic that many now view management’s philanthropic acts as a problem. The modem debate over corporations’ social responsibility began with claims that corporations gave too little, not too much. Challenging the prevailing views of the time in an important and then-controversial article, Milton Friedman argued that acts of pure corporate philanthropy (i.e., philanthropy inconsistent with maximizing a firm’s profits) were a mere waste of shareholders’ assets and thus contrary to management’s function. Friedman must be pleasantly surprised to find contemporary mainstream commentators worrying about the same waste of assets that concerned him. Nevertheless, current newspaper stories about corporate philanthropy are more likely to praise the “giant corporation” for demonstrating “social responsibility” through liberal philanthropy.

This paper explores the “problem of corporate philanthropy” from the standpoint of the contractual theory of the firm. That is, it considers corporate philanthropy within a framework of the types of contracts that shareholders generally would find desirable to govern relations among themselves and between shareholders and managers. Part I explains this general framework, noting in particular that shareholders desire the firm to assume only those functions that the firm can perform better (or more cheaply) than individuals themselves could undertake them.

This desire explains why investors want their firms to make some sorts of charitable donations but not others, as Part II discusses. But to achieve the benefits of corporate philanthropy, investors who leave philanthropic decisions to firm management must countenance the possibility that management’s own objectives, not those of shareholders, may motivate some philanthropy. This problem is no different, however, from any other agency cost that shareholders willingly confront when they choose to invest in firms that have a split between ownership and control. Thus, the reasons for a separate literature on philanthropy (often calling for separate legal rules to regulate the “problem” of philanthropy) remain obscure.

Part III explores these concepts of philanthropy against the backdrop of the recent suggestion that corporate philanthropy is different from the other agency costs that shareholders must tolerate in exchange for others running their firm. Invoking the team production explanation of firms, some suggest that managers ought to be able to support charity in ways that do not maximize firm profits and that the law recognizes the desirability of unprofitable philanthropy. Part III argues against both the claims that corporate philanthropic giving unrelated to firm profitability is desirable and that the law validates it.

title: The Impact of AI on Innovation and Operational Efficiencies for Small to Medium Enterprises

detail.title: The Impact of AI on Innovation and Operational Efficiencies for Small to Medium Enterprises
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming industrial operations for small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) by reducing downtime, optimizing production, and driving innovation. However, success depends not merely on adopting AI but on executing structured implementation strategies. This study examines how SMEs can effectively deploy AI to enhance operational efficiency, reduce waste, and improve product quality. Using qualitative analysis and realworld case studies, the research compares structured versus unstructured AI adoption across SMEs. Preliminary findings reveal that structured approaches-characterized by phased rollouts, workforce training, and real-time performance tracking-yield superior outcomes in machinery uptime, energy use, and quality assurance. The study also highlights the importance of human-AI collaboration, where AI augments rather than replaces human expertise. Drawing from success stories like Deep Seek, the paper outlines best practices for AI adoption, emphasizing the role of strategic integration. The findings contribute actionable insights for SMEs aiming to leverage AI as a catalyst for sustainable growth and operational excellence.

title: Can Strategic Agent Manipulation Break Hybrid Recommender-Based Rebalancing? A Computational Study for One-Way Carsharing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Can Strategic Agent Manipulation Break Hybrid Recommender-Based Rebalancing? A Computational Study for One-Way Carsharing
detail.abstract: One-way carsharing systems increasingly rely on hybrid recommender systems-combining collaborative filtering with contextual information such as real-time vehicle availability and parking occupancy-to suggest pickup and drop-off locations to users. While these recommenders improve utilization, their vulnerability to strategic manipulation remains unexplored. This paper investigates whether malicious users can deliberately bias hybrid recommendations to disrupt fleet rebalancing operations. We formulate a computational attack model where strategic agents inject fake trip ratings or selective booking requests, aiming to artificially inflate demand for specific stations. Using a simulation framework calibrated with real-world carsharing trip data (2015-2016), we evaluate three hybrid recommender variants (weighted, switching, and feature-augmented) under increasing attack intensities. Our results show that even low-level manipulation (5-10% of trips) can shift recommended station ranks significantly, causing the subsequent rebalancing algorithm-a greedy relocation heuristic common in practice-to reposition vehicles into suboptimal locations. Under a sustained 15% attack, total empty vehicle miles increase by up to 34% compared to the non-adversarial baseline, while user waiting times at non-targeted stations rise by over 40 minutes per day. We further propose two computationally lightweight defenses: rating clipping and temporal decay of older interactions, which together reduce manipulation impact by 61% without retraining the recommender. To our knowledge, this is the first study to quantify the vulnerability of hybrid recommender-based rebalancing in one-way carsharing under strategic manipulation, with direct implications for system operators deploying collaborative filtering in mobility platforms.

detail.abstract: The companion paper demonstrates that aggregate optimization structurally produces alignment failures through five mechanisms: three system failures (substitution, topology blindness, complexity foresight) and two agent exploitations of those failures (compensation, topology reshaping). This paper presents Agency Calculus (AC), a floor optimization architecture designed to address all five. AC has five components: agency as the optimization primitive, the POLI-EH measurement framework with concrete operationalization, the dual-objective architecture (JAM as the safety constraint for AI alignment, Nash welfare as the governance objective for human systems), a three-rule governance layer mapped one-to-one onto the three system failures, and an applied economic layer (REACH). The paper addresses the measurement problem directly by specifying what each POLI dimension tracks at the individual level, what proxy measurements are available, and how a privacy-preserving personal computation architecture avoids the failures of aggregate metrics like GDP. The applied layer, REACH, translates AC into engineering constraints including an anti-gaming architecture that makes metric manipulation a dominated strategy through hidden cross-pair verification. A worked example demonstrates the full architecture operating on a concrete scenario.

title: Analysis of the Bullwhip Effect in the Apparel Supply Chain: A Multi-Level Perspective from Bangladesh

detail.title: Analysis of the Bullwhip Effect in the Apparel Supply Chain: A Multi-Level Perspective from Bangladesh
detail.abstract: This research examines the Bullwhip Effect within the apparel supply chain of Bangladesh, focusing on both manufacturing and distribution perspectives. Using a cumulative buffer model, the study illustrates how an initial demand of 330 units can escalate to a production requirement of 500 units due to a lack of information transparency. Through a case study at Apex Holdings Limited, the paper analyzes the impact of "overrun" stock and proposes inventory recovery strategies. Additionally, a "Reverse Bullwhip" is identified within localized dealership networks. The findings suggest that collaborative forecasting and reduced lead times are essential for mitigating these inefficiencies and enhancing the global competitiveness of the Bangladesh textile sector.

detail.abstract: This academic report provides a comprehensive analysis of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as the cornerstone of the Fourth Industrial Revolution and its profound impact on the global business environment. The study explores core AI technologies—including Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, and Computer Vision—detailing their strategic integration into key business functions such as marketing, human resources, and supply chain logistics. By evaluating the shift from "Narrow AI" to autonomous "Agentic Systems," the paper highlights significant benefits in operational efficiency and data-driven decision-making. The report concludes that AI is no longer an optional innovation but a fundamental infrastructure, requiring a balanced "human-in-the-loop" strategy to navigate the complexities of the 2026 corporate landscape.

title: THE TARIFF BASKET: A Currency-Board Analogue for Electricity Regulation in Small Open Economies

detail.title: THE TARIFF BASKET: A Currency-Board Analogue for Electricity Regulation in Small Open Economies
detail.abstract: This working paper establishes conceptual and empirical priority for the following original contributions: 1. The Tariff Basket concept: a normative regulatory instrument for electricity pricing in small open economies, defined as the trade-weighted average of industrial electricity tariffs of key trading partners. Distinct from benchmark regulation in that it grounds the reference level in bilateral trade weights and applies as a binding sustainability constraint. 2. Tariff Sustainability Condition (Proposition 1): a formalization proving that a tariff below T_basket * (1-delta) is inherently unstable, triggering fiscal collapse or asset degradation. No prior work in energy regulation has formalized an equivalent equilibrium condition. 3. Competitive Advantage Discount (delta): an operationalized methodology for estimating the maximum sustainable downward deviation from the basket, grounded in LCOE differentials. Applied to Kyrgyzstan: delta = 0.20-0.25, minimum sustainable industrial tariff 5.7 c/kWh vs. actual 4.35 c/kWh (2024). 4. Illustrative panel evidence for Central Asia (2010-2024): a fixed-effects regression across three economies showing that a 1 c/kWh increase in the tariff gap is associated with a 28-34% reduction in generation investment.

detail.abstract: Institutions deploying artificial intelligence into decision workflows do not fail because of underperforming models. They fail because of broken governance structures around them. This position paper formalizes The Workflow Thesis — a three-layer Operational Playbook hierarchy comprising Governance, Protocols, and Work Processes — as the structural architecture institutions must build before any model is procured. The Thesis argues that compliance activity is not governance structure; that policy without architecture is theater; and that the system itself, not the model, is the safety mechanism. The framework is designed for federal agencies, regulated enterprises, and higher-education institutions deploying AI under operational, legal, or reputational pressure. The paper situates the framework within current AI governance regimes (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001), introduces the Workflow Thesis Diagnostic instrument, applies the framework to a documented institutional failure case (Air Canada, 2024), and concludes by positioning the Workflow Thesis as the operational complement to the author's earlier work on the pedagogy of AI governance.

title: Data Set-Spatiotemporal Bikeshare System Status
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business, Howard University School of Business and University of Virginia

detail.title: Data Set-Spatiotemporal Bikeshare System Status

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Problem Definition: Bikeshare systems are expanding worldwide, but empirical research is hindered by the lack of high-frequency data on system status. Public bikeshare datasets typically include only trip start and end records, with no information on real-time station conditions (e.g., how many bikes or docks are available). This gap in data limits the analysis of operational performance and user service levels in bikeshare systems. Methodology/Results: We address this gap by collecting nearly minute-by-minute status data from Washington, D.C.'s Capital Bikeshare system over a three-year period (April 2019-September 2022). For each station and minute in this dataset, we record the number of available bikes and open docks, along with station location details. We also include data on dockless bikes introduced during the collection period. The raw data were cleaned to correct errors and can be connected to official trip records data. This high resolution dataset enables direct measurement of system performance. For example, analysis of August 2022 shows that bikes were completely unavailable (bike stockout) for approximately 1.94% of station-minutes, while all docks were occupied (dock stockout) for about 0.78% of station-minutes. We also propose a method for using the data to identify potential rebalance events. Managerial Implications: The availability of this granular status data opens new avenues for empirical research and decision-making in operations management. Researchers and practitioners can leverage it to improve demand forecasting models, design more effective rebalancing strategies for bike distribution, and rigorously measure system performance (e.g., availability and stockouts) over time. By providing previously unavailable insights into full system status, this dataset supports more informed operational planning and real-time management of bikeshare services.

title: The Lovelace Threshold: A Governance Diagnostic Beyond Bounded Systems

detail.title: The Lovelace Threshold: A Governance Diagnostic Beyond Bounded Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This is the conceptual foundation of the body of work created by the author who runs a practitioner-led research and consultation to creates conditions for leaders to investigate systemic vulnerabilities from inside the systems they're responsible for.
declarations.funderStatement: This work is unfunded.

contentFormat.other: Supplemental note for Security-by-design: A Case for Digital Rights Enforcement Through Data Pipeline Attestations

detail.abstract:
The Lovelace Threshold is a conceptual diagnostic device that exposes where the assumptions of current governance frameworks no longer match the operational logic of generative and autonomous systems. It names the point at which a governance mechanism stops being reliable because it was designed for a world in which a governed system is fully legible, fully bounded, and fully predictable in advance. In such settings, rules can be written around visible governable bodies. That's the Lovelace World, where systems merely execute predefined instructions. But now systems have evolved, we can recombine, or generate downstream effects that exceed explicit specification, and visible governance becomes structurally insufficient. That's the Post-Lovelace World, where systems anticipate, generate, and act beyond explicit specification. The gap between the two is a structural vulnerability that operates beyond current political frameworks' reach. This short note argues that the threshold applies beyond AI to any governance regime that depends on incomplete visibility into the substrate it seeks to regulate. The remedy is not only better after-the-fact enforcement, but upstream controls grounded in provenance, transformation accountability, and verifiable attestation.

title: Heterogeneous Pricing of Supply Chain Risk in Production Networks

detail.title: Heterogeneous Pricing of Supply Chain Risk in Production Networks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
